text: Your hands volunteer before your name does. Hasta's first quarter takes Aries in the navamsa, the ninth division of the chart that deals each quarter its sign, and the mansion's skill arrives at speed here: the jammed door shouldered open, the split lip iced, the crashed file rebuilt while its owner is still apologizing. Savitar, the golden god who presides over Hasta, is the impeller of the old hymns, the one who sets the day's work moving, and your quarter inherits the setting-in-motion more than the finishing. First drafts, first aid, first tries: beginnings obey you. The trouble hides in other people's fumbling. Watching an unpracticed hand struggle with a task you could end in seconds is nearly physical pain for you, so you take the knife, the wheel, the keyboard, and the person you rescued learns mainly to stand aside. A skill taken over is a skill nobody gains. Your quickness turns teacherly on the day you can keep your hands in your pockets through someone's slow, wrong, necessary first attempt, and the apprentices you manage not to rescue are the ones who come back doing it your way, faster than you.

Repetition is where your gift lives. The same knot tied a thousand times, the scale practiced until the fingers own it, the dough turned every cold morning: Hasta's second quarter builds skill the slow way, into muscle, where nothing can talk it out of you. Taurus holds this stretch of the ninth-harmonic chart, and it gives the mansion's clever hands patience and a price list; what you make is solid, and you usually know what it is worth. Crafts feed you here, sometimes literally: food, fabric, wood, massage, gardens, any trade where quality can be judged with the eyes closed. The same practice that puts a skill beyond thought can put the day beyond it too. Hands this well trained keep going while you are somewhere else, so an afternoon of good work can pass with nobody home behind it, and Hasta's restlessness hides easily inside a craft. The work stays honest either way. A thousand repetitions are hard to fake, and the people who buy from you once tend to buy from you for life.

Hasta's emblem is an open hand, and in the third quarter it pairs up: two hands trading the work between them, the way a juggler's do. Gemini is this quarter's seat in the navamsa, the chart's ninth division, and a pair of hands that already worked fast picks up a commentary. You learn crafts the way other people pick up gossip, quickly and from every direction: a repair watched once and repeated, a recipe followed from across the room, the printer fixed while you hold a phone call that has nothing to do with printers. Explaining comes bundled with doing. You teach whatever your hands know, often mid-task, and any kitchen or workshop with you in it turns into a running clinic. Demonstration comes so easily that it can replace apprenticeship. You get good enough to show, then wander to the next skill, and ten trades can sit in your hands at journeyman depth while mastery waits in none of them. The pattern meets its match in the first craft that refuses to be charming, the instrument or language or trade that stays awkward past the point where you would normally leave. Staying clumsy at one thing on purpose, a full season past the expiry date of your interest, is the strangest work this quarter ever takes on, and it is how one hand ends up teaching the other something neither could pick up fast.

When someone you love is hurting, you cook. Or you mend the coat they keep meaning to throw out, reset the crooked shelf, arrive with a toolbox where other people arrive with words. The last quarter of Hasta bends the mansion's skill toward keeping people, and its ninth-division sign, Cancer, turns the household into the workshop: your care has calluses, and the people around you live better in a hundred small ways they have mostly stopped noticing. Hair gets braided, lunches packed, the fever watched through the night with a practical calm that is itself a comfort. Work that holds and handles at once fits you well: nursing, bodywork, teaching small children, kitchens of every kind. The restlessness that runs through this mansion turns domestic in you, and so does its wish to manage whatever it touches. A worried evening becomes a reorganized pantry. A fight you do not know how to finish becomes a repaired fence, the apology built instead of said, which works right up until the person needed the sentence more than the shelf. Some of what your people carry cannot be fixed, only heard, and there your hands, for once, are the wrong tool. Sitting beside a problem you are not allowed to touch may be the hardest labor this quarter is ever handed. The ones who stay long enough learn to read you anyway; the soup says what you meant. Now and then somebody sets the towel down for you, takes the chair across the table, and just waits, and from that side of it you learn what the hour is worth.

Everything you make gets signed, whether or not your name is on it. Chitra's first quarter cannot ship anonymous work: the cut of a sentence, the plating of a dinner, the spacing on a slide all carry your handwriting, and you would rather redo a thing at midnight than let a sloppy version circulate wearing your fingerprints. The ninth-harmonic chart hands this quarter to Leo, and the mansion's craft steps into daylight with it: you want the unveiling, the opening night, the moment the cloth comes off. Tvashtar, Chitra's presiding artificer, forged the thunderbolt Indra carries into battle, work made to be seen in use, and your best pieces have that same quality of public function, beautiful and load-bearing at once. Because the work is signed, though, every note lands on skin. A client's casual edit can ache for days, and you have defended a font the way other people defend a border. The work is not your face, however much handwriting it carries, and revision gets fast and cheap the moment a critique stops sounding like a verdict. The pieces that survive many hands, it turns out, still come out looking like yours.

The better version is usually a smaller fix than anyone expects: a seam moved half an inch, one adjective cut, the shelf lowered two holes. Chitra's second quarter works at millimeter scale, and Virgo, its seat in the navamsa, the chart's ninth part, gives the mansion's designing eye the patience to execute quietly. Restorers, editors, tailors, and debuggers live in this quarter, along with whoever the family calls when the beautiful thing breaks. The eye never fully closes, and pointed at yourself it becomes a punch list with no completion date: posture, vocabulary, morning routine, all under permanent renovation. A house has to be lived in during the remodel, and so do you. The rooms you have already made right are pleasant places, and you visit them less than anyone you love would wish.

A jewel is Chitra's emblem, and any jeweler will say the secret is the setting: the stone is half the art, and the mount is what lets it be worn. Your quarter designs settings. Rooms arranged so that conversation has somewhere to land, dinners cast like ensembles, a friend's rough news framed so the family can actually hear it: the mansion's brilliance turns relational under Libra in the ninth division of the chart, and what you compose is occasions. People relax inside your arrangements without knowing why. Couples ask you to shape their weddings, offices their gatherings, and you have a knack for making other people look finer than they knew they could, which is a more generous art than shining alone. The polish can become the thing it was hiding. An evening can be staged so gracefully that nothing true survives it, and a relationship's appearance, the photos, the dinners, the public ease, can stay curated for years while the real conversation waits in a drawer. Beauty in this mansion was always meant to bear weight. A setting that can hold an argument is finer work than one that can only hold a photograph, and the evenings people remember longest are the ones something true happened inside.

Chitra's last quarter does not redecorate; it guts. Under Scorpio in the ninth-harmonic chart, the mansion's appetite for the better version goes down to the studs: you are drawn to the projects other designers refuse, the house with the cracked foundation, the failing department, the life that must be taken apart to be saved, and you work best behind a closed door with the plans held close. Depth is what gives your taste its edge. Where the rest of this mansion improves surfaces, you can smell what is wrong inside a structure, a business, a person, and your sense of what has to go is usually severe and usually right. You apply the method to yourself without telling anyone. A year of quiet demolition, and you resurface with a new body, a new trade, a new way of speaking, each finished self presented as if it had always stood there. The vanished middle is what the secrecy costs. Friends keep meeting your afters and never your durings, so their love attaches to versions, and some part of you concludes the love was earned by the finish rather than the person. It was not. A demolition run alone also has nobody in it to say which wall was load-bearing, which is the practical cost of the secrecy sitting on top of the private one, and the projects that came out best were the ones with a witness in the dust.

Your restlessness has a heading. Swati's first quarter draws Sagittarius from the navamsa, the ninth division of the sidereal chart, and the mansion's wind picks up a compass: where your kin drift on whatever current is local, you are pulled by the far thing, the border, the degree program, the discipline with a mountain at the end of it. Vayu, the wind god who presides over Swati, is in the old hymns the fastest of the gods and the breath in every body, everywhere at once and held nowhere, and your quarter carries his range. You cover ground, in miles or in reading, that steadier people cannot credit. Distance is also this quarter's favorite anesthetic. A goal on the horizon can justify perpetual motion, the itinerary grows a new leg whenever the current one nears its end, and it is possible to travel for a decade in a way that changes your scenery more than your mind. The trips that count are the ones that cost you a conviction. You can tell within a day of coming home: the bags empty quickly, and one belief did not survive the journey.

Self-employment, in some form or other, is where this quarter tends to end up, whatever the business card says. Swati's second quarter keeps the mansion's need for open air and adds the discipline to build with it: schedules kept without a boss, money managed across lean months, the trader's instinct run like a firm. In the ninth division this stretch of Swati passes through Capricorn, and under it the mansion's light touch learns to sign leases. You negotiate patiently, deliver on the day, and quietly decline every rope anyone throws you, including the useful ones. Help reads to you as supervision, delegation as risk, and you will carry a workload built for three before you let a second pair of hands near the controls. The business, or the household run like one, grows to the exact size one untethered person can hold. Its next size needs a hire, a partner, or a favor accepted, and accepting is the skill this quarter prices slowest.

Swati's emblem is a young shoot that bends in wind, and the third quarter plants it in a field of others: the co-op, the collective, the union, the scene. You do groups the way the shoot does weather, present, responsive, never quite bent out of your own shape. Aquarius governs this quarter in the ninth-harmonic chart, and it suits the mansion's oldest talent, which is staying free inside systems. You can work a bureaucracy, a friend group, or a movement without being captured by any of them. Rooms full of strong opinions relax around your unpushy one, and you are often the member everyone likes and nobody can quite count on for Thursday. Commitment triggers the same reflex in you as a hand closing around the stem. You answer it the mansion's way, not by refusing but by drifting: fewer meetings, softer replies, membership thinning. Someone finally asks whether you have left, and you realize you did, months ago, without ever deciding to. The exits cost more than they show. Scenes remember who slipped away, and the belonging you actually want keeps having to be restarted from zero somewhere new. Annoyance is the weather your quarter has never sat through, and it is most of what a lasting group is made of; the people who irritate you in year three are the ones who still know your name in year ten.

Nobody has ever felt crowded by you. The fourth quarter of Swati gives the mansion's airiness its gentlest form: you hold opinions without pressing them, love without monitoring, and enter rooms the way weather changes, gradually and without demands. Pisces closes the mansion's run through the ninth division, and the trader's lightness turns there into something nearer to grace: people exhale around you, tell you things early, and mend a little faster with you nearby, mostly because you are the one person not steering them. The same softness blurs your edges. Your yes is quiet and your no is silence, so the difference between drifting and leaving can be invisible even to you: engagements fade rather than end, and someone who loves you can spend a whole winter unsure whether you are gone. Vagueness is the one unkindness a person this gentle can be fairly accused of. The freedom you hand out so generously is only worth what people can locate. They have to know where they stand inside it before it reads to them as freedom at all.

You enlist the way other people browse. A cause, a course, a company: wanting arrives all at once and fully armed in Vishakha's first quarter, and the gap between deciding and starting shrinks to an afternoon. Aries holds the quarter's place in the navamsa, the chart's ninth division, and it puts the mansion's two patrons briefly in agreement, Indra the king who orders the campaign and Agni the fire that lights it, both wide awake in you on day one. Day one is your masterpiece. The January gym, the venture's first quarter, the opening months of a courtship: nobody outworks you early, and your conviction recruits people before you have finished explaining it. This mansion runs campaigns that are long by design, and your quarter provisions them like sprints. The fire that declared the war wants the victory parade by spring, boredom lands hardest in the unphotographed middle years, and you can catch yourself launching fresh crusades for the spark of them while three half-won ones wait for supplies. Vishakha keeps its promises across decades. Yours will arrive early or not at all until pacing gets learned like any other drill: a fire kept deliberately small, still lit in year six, when the first charge is only a story you tell.

Long campaigns are won by supply lines, and yours is the quarter that builds them. Vishakha's second quarter turns the mansion's persistence into stores: savings that grow without drama, tools bought once and kept sharp, a body and a routine maintained like equipment the goal will need in year four. Taurus anchors this stretch in the ninth division of the chart, and the mansion's fire slows into endurance: you may be the least flashy of Vishakha's quarters and the hardest to stop. The stores have a way of becoming the campaign. Provisioning is real work, and it is also the safest work, so the reserve keeps growing while the march it was gathered for stays a plan: another season of tools, another season of training, the number in the account rising with no date set against it. Readiness can be held indefinitely, which is exactly what makes it comfortable. Vishakha banked its fire in this quarter rather than putting it out, and a campaign this well supplied can afford to move before it feels ready.

Vishakha's emblem is an arch, and an arch stands on two legs. Your quarter, the third, keeps trying to raise each leg as its own tower. This stretch belongs to Gemini in the ninth-harmonic chart, which doubles a mansion already named for branching: beside every main campaign of yours a second one grows, real, funded with actual hours, never quite a hobby. You are also the herald. Recruiting allies, pitching, keeping backers warm: you can describe the finished gateway so vividly that whole rooms sign on before the foundation is poured. Watch what happens in the middles. Every long effort has one, the flat stretch with no applause in it, and your habit is to greet that stretch by crossing to the other project, which is always, conveniently, still in its thrilling first mile. The crossing feels like diligence, because you are never idle. Both builds simply stay early, year after year, and the choice this mansion finds so painful gets postponed by commuting between beginnings. One finished leg changes the whole arithmetic. The dormant project keeps better than the urgent voice in you insists, and completion turns out to transfer: the second tower rises in half the time once your hands have raised a first.

Somewhere behind every long effort of yours there is a kitchen table and the people who sit at it. Vishakha's last quarter points the mansion's persistence at private life: the mortgage cleared for a family, the degree finished with a child watching, the decade of shifts worked so that somebody else's future gets wider. Cancer receives this quarter in the ninth division, and the campaign moves indoors: where your kin want the title or the summit, you want the secured home, the parents settled, the household nobody can take away. Loyalty at this depth is its own kind of formidable. You do not leave people mid-campaign, you remember what was promised at the beginning, and families run for a generation on the ground that one such member wins for them. The mansion's scorekeeping follows you indoors, and private life starts to carry finish lines: engaged by this year, a house by that one, children hitting milestones on schedule. A cousin's kitchen renovation can spoil your week the way a rival's promotion spoils your kin's. A home that is being measured is not quite being lived in. The evening you spend tallying where the household ought to be by now is an evening the household spent without you. The campaigns are real, and the roof really is needed. Some part of every year already counts as the life the struggle was for, though, and the ones who love you can point to it faster than you can, usually while pulling out a chair.
